answer: Cap each agent behind a staked identity bond: to act, an account must post a deposit proportional to its influence, and that deposit is slashed if peers catch it colluding. A Sybil attacker who splits into a thousand puppets must fund a thousand bonds out of pocket, so one unit of voting power costs real capital rather than a fresh keypair. The economics flip: burning a whisper of trust now requires facing a public ledge of locked collateral, and votes near an oasis of shared liquidity must be backed by the same. Attacking costs more than the reward, so the cheap clone army never forms.
